# Candidate crystals
- Crystal-K3: inorganic scintillator, high light yield, fast decay.
- Crystal-K1: inorganic scintillator, medium light yield.
- Crystal-K2: inorganic scintillator, mature growth process, lower light yield.
All three are available in the required sizes from at least one vendor.

Energy resolution at 662 keV (FWHM): Crystal-K3 2.9%, Crystal-K1 4.5%, Crystal-K2 8.5%.
Thickness dependence was weak in the 3-8 cm range.

# Meeting notes 2026-02-11
Attendees discussed the shielding upgrade (lead + copper, complete) and the schedule for commissioning in Q3. Action: finalise the crystal choice this quarter.

# Shielding status
The 20 cm lead + 5 cm OFHC copper castle is installed. Radon purge with boil-off nitrogen is operational.

content.text:
I read all six project documents. None of them gives intrinsic background rates for the three crystals, so the 0.5 counts/kg/day budget can't be checked yet.

- **Candidates (`candidate_specs.md`):** The descriptions are qualitative only.
  - K3: high light yield, fast decay.
  - K1: medium light yield.
  - K2: mature growth process, lower light yield.
- **Resolution (`simulation_summary_2025.md`):** At 662 keV and 5 cm, FWHM is 2.9% for K3, 4.5% for K1 and 8.5% for K2. Thickness dependence was weak between 3 and 8 cm.
- **Budget:** The 0.5 counts/kg/day limit appears only in the task brief, not in any document.
- **Other documents:** The shielding (20 cm lead plus 5 cm copper, radon purge running) reduces external background, not the crystals' intrinsic background. The DAQ plan needs no change for any crystal. Procurement is scheduled for Q2.
- **Mass scaling:** Nothing says how background was measured or how it scales with mass.

On resolution alone K3 would be the choice. I did not assume it meets the background limit, because that is unverified for all three crystals. Background data from the vendors or an assay is needed before recommending a crystal.

I recorded all of this with `record_results`.

I ran all 15 simulations (3 crystals × 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 cm) and recorded the results. None of the three crystals is confirmed to meet the background limit, so these numbers say nothing about compliance.

The earlier steps found no intrinsic-background data for any crystal. Because of that, no crystal was known to be ineligible, so I simulated all three. I treated the runs as resolution data only.

FWHM at 662 keV (%):

| Thickness | K3 | K1 | K2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 cm | 3.377 | 5.052 | 9.469 |
| 4 cm | 2.960 | 4.648 | 8.972 |
| 6 cm | 2.991 | 4.565 | 8.631 |
| 8 cm | 3.262 | 4.920 | 9.856 |
| 10 cm | 4.122 | 6.315 | 11.543 |

- **Thickness:** Each crystal does best at about 4–6 cm. Resolution is clearly worse at 2 cm and gets much worse at 10 cm.
- **K3:** K3 has the best resolution at every thickness. Its 4 cm and 6 cm values (2.960% and 2.991%) are within noise of each other.
- **Consistency:** The results agree with the 2025 values at 5 cm.
- **Provisional pick:** If a pick is forced, K3 at about 4–6 cm is the provisional choice. It stays conditional on vendor or assay background data for each crystal.
- **Grid:** The thickness grid is coarse. A finer scan between 3 and 7 cm could refine the optimum.

content.text:
I ran seven more simulations and recorded the results. Resolution is best at about 5 cm for all three crystals. I still could not check the background budget for any of them.

**Resolution (FWHM % at 662 keV)**

| Crystal | Best thickness | Best FWHM | Other thicknesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| K3 | 5 cm | 2.923% | 3 cm: 3.053; 7 cm: 2.988 |
| K1 | 5 cm | 4.408% | 7 cm: 4.858 |
| K2 | 5 cm | 8.559% | 7 cm: 8.817 |

- **K3 across all runs:** The full set of K3 values is 3.377% at 2 cm, 3.053% at 3 cm, 2.960% at 4 cm, 2.923% at 5 cm, 2.991% at 6 cm, 2.988% at 7 cm, 3.262% at 8 cm and 4.122% at 10 cm.
- **Trend:** Resolution is not monotonic in thickness. It has a broad optimum around 4–6 cm. It is worse at 2 cm and much worse beyond 8 cm, probably because thicker crystals lose more light.
- **How firm the optimum is:** Within 4–7 cm the K3 values differ by only about 0.05%, which is close to the noise. So 5 cm is the best single point, but 4–6 cm is effectively equivalent.
- **Ranking:** K3 beats K1, and K1 beats K2, at every thickness.

**Background budget:** No document gives an intrinsic background for any crystal, or says how it scales with mass or size. I therefore could not verify the 0.5 counts/kg/day limit at 5 cm or at any other thickness. Mass grows with thickness, so total counts per day would also grow. No crystal is verified as eligible.

K3 at about 5 cm is only a provisional choice based on resolution. Any recommendation has to be conditional on vendor or assay background data for K3, with K1 as the fallback.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Crystal-K3 at 5 cm. This is provisional, and I could not check it against the background limit.**

- **Resolution:** The simulated FWHM at 662 keV is 2.923%, the best of any crystal and thickness.
- **Background versus budget:** No project document gives an intrinsic background rate (100–3000 keV) for any crystal, so K3's background is unknown. I re-read `candidate_specs.md` and the meeting notes, and both are qualitative only. The 0.5 counts/kg/day budget appears only in the task brief. I did not relax the hard requirement, and I can't call K3 compliant. Vendor or assay data in counts/kg/day is needed before Q2 procurement.

**Runner-up options**
- **Thickness:** K3 at 4 cm gives 2.960% and at 6 cm gives 2.991%. Both are equivalent to 5 cm within the simulation noise of about 0.05%.
- **Fallback crystal:** If K3 fails the background check, use K1 at 5 cm (4.408%). K2 at 5 cm is the last choice (8.559%).

**Caveats**
- **Simulation only:** The result is simulation-only, with no experimental validation.
- **Thickness:** Avoid 10 cm (K3 gives 4.122%) and 2 cm (K3 gives 3.377%).
- **Exclusions:** I excluded no candidates, so none was ruled out.
- **Document gaps:** The documents give no background figures, no units and no mass or thickness scaling. It is unclear whether the budget applies per kg or per crystal, and mass grows with thickness.
- **Timing:** The meeting notes say to finalise the crystal choice this quarter. Commissioning is in Q3.

I recorded all of this with `record_results`.
